events.comment: Combat_Shared: rules used by every fight. Each scene needs an Enemy group and an EnemyHitbox group, and links this sheet before that boss's own events. Every EnemyHitbox object needs Damage, HasHit and IsMelee variables.
Arena fade-in: every fight (and the tutorial) opens from black: a short hold, then a smooth fade of about a second.

inlineCode: // Arena fade-in: the fight opens from black instead of cutting in. A black sheet over the whole screen (on the
// scene's own top container, so the camera doesn't move it, and it works in scenes without a UI layer) holds for
// HOLD seconds, hiding the first frames while things settle, then fades out over FADE seconds and is removed.
const st = runtimeScene.__arenaFade || (runtimeScene.__arenaFade = { t: 0, sheet: null, done: false });
// Real frame time, capped so a long first (loading) frame doesn't skip the fade.
const k = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (st.t - HOLD) / FADE));
st.sheet.alpha = 1 - k * k * (3 - 2 * k); // Smoothstep: eases in and out.
if (k >= 1) { st.sheet.parent && st.sheet.parent.removeChild(st.sheet); st.sheet.destroy(); st.sheet = null; st.done = true; }

events.comment: Scene start: remember the uncursed max HP and set up the bar maximums. (Where the bars sit is the fight UI layout's job, further down.)

Brand budget: on the first frame of a fight, the brands the player has earned take max HP (BrandBudget / N each, never below the HP floor) and the Cat's mercy adds a life. Not in the tutorial. The curse stacks of this fight work on top of it.

inlineCode: // Brand budget (docs/design-brand-mercy.md, phase 2). Runs once, on the first frame of a fight, after the scene start event has set
// Player.BaseMaxHealth. It applies what the player has permanently earned, from the globals the hub fills in (BrandCount, BossCount,
// BonusLives): each brand costs BrandBudget / N of the base max HP (BrandFraction), never below the HP floor (HpFloorPercent), and the Cat's
// mercy adds a life. The curse stacks are the fight's own (events in this sheet: Player loses a life, Curse removal) and work on top of it.
// The tutorial is practice: no brands, no bonus lives. With no hub counts (a scene opened straight from the editor) nothing changes.
const gn = k => g.get(k).getAsNumber(), pn = k => pv.get(k).getAsNumber();
const fraction = Math.round(pn("BrandBudget") / 100 * gn("BrandCount") / n * 10000) / 10000;   // Rounded so the floor check below has no float noise.
const base = pn("BaseMaxHealth"), floor = base * pn("HpFloorPercent") / 100;

events.comment: Composure: while the player is above ComposureBand of max HP (and the hub says he has mercy), Poise (mercy 1) raises stamina regen, Respite (mercy 2) refunds stamina on a perfect deflect, Steady hand (mercy 3) widens the perfect-deflect window, and Grace (mercy 5) makes hits cost less of his posture. It works out StaminaRegenNow, PerfectFractionNow and PostureTakenNow for the events that read them. Not in the tutorial.

inlineCode: // Composure (docs/design-brand-mercy.md, phase 5): the mercy tree's passives, which work only while the player is at HIGH HP (more than
// ComposureBand of max HP, so one small mistake does not turn them off). Runs every frame, early in Combat_Shared, and works out the values the
// other events read, the way Desperation does with DeflectWindowNow:
//   Poise        (mercy 1): StaminaRegenNow = the regen rate plus PoiseBonus (the stamina regen event reads it).
//   Respite      (mercy 2): a new perfect deflect refunds RespiteStamina stamina (reads PerfectCount with its own seen number).
//   Steady hand  (mercy 3): PerfectFractionNow = the perfect window plus SteadyHandBonus (the perfect deflect events read it).
//   Grace        (mercy 5): PostureTakenNow = 1 minus GraceBonus (the two places where the player's posture goes up read it: a hit in Combat_Shared and the
//                Gunslinger's bullet), so hits cost less of his own posture.
// MercyCount is a global the hub fills in. The tutorial is practice: no passives. Light step (4) is in tools/powers/dodge.js.
const on = mercy > 0 && max > 0 && pn("Health") / max > pn("ComposureBand") && !pv.get("IsDead").getAsBoolean();
if (count < st.seen) st.seen = count;                                   // The count was reset (a new fight).
pv.get("DashCharges").setNumber(Math.min(pn("DashChargesMax"), pn("DashCharges") + 1));   // And a dash charge back (only matters with the Flash step).

events.comment: Brand passives: Riposte (brand 2): a new perfect deflect sends the player's SHADOW (Player_Shadow: a dark double, tools/fx/player_shadow.js) to the boss, so the player himself stays free to punish. The script spawns it and, when its slash lands, sets Player.RiposteStrike; the events below find the boss for it and do the damage: RiposteMult times AttackDamage off the enemy's health (never its posture). Not in the tutorial.

inlineCode: // The Brand tree's passives (docs/design-brand-mercy.md, phase 5), the first one: Riposte (brand 2). Runs every frame, after the Composure script in
// Combat_Shared. SHADOW ECHO (brand 1) comes after the Riposte part below. The player's SHADOW counters for him, so he is free to punish with his own attack. The steps:
//   1. A NEW perfect MELEE deflect (Player.PerfectMeleeCount, which tools/perfect counts for melee attacks only: the Samurai's tornado, Judgement Cut and
//      Thousand Cuts, arrows, petals and grenades never call the shadow), above this script's own seen number, the way every power reads it) sets Player.RiposteFire to 1 when
//      the hub says the player has 2 or more brands (BrandCount, a global).
//   2. The first event below (it can see the Enemy group) writes the boss's x into Player.RiposteX and sets RiposteFire to 2.

//   3. Here, RiposteFire 2 spawns Player_Shadow (tools/fx/player_shadow.js) on a RANDOM side of the boss (a side with a wall in the way is not picked; with walls on both sides, no shadow comes), facing him, and starts its clock.
//   4. At STRIKE seconds (the slash arc of its frame 3) this sets Player.RiposteStrike to 1; the next event takes RiposteMult times AttackDamage of
//      health off the enemy (never posture), with the player's hit sound and blood (from Player.RiposteSrcX, where the shadow stood), and clears it.
//   5. The shadow flickers while it lasts, fades out over its last FADE seconds and is deleted. Not in the tutorial; the player dying clears it.
const GAP = 80;                                                          // Px between the boss's centre and the shadow's body.
const STRIKE = 0.14, LIFE = 0.5, FADE = 0.2, ALPHA = 215;                // Seconds to the cut, seconds alive, the fade at the end, the opacity at full.
const player = players[0], pv = player.getVariables(), g = runtimeScene.getGame().getVariables();
const st = runtimeScene.__brandPassives || (runtimeScene.__brandPassives = { seen: count, shadows: [] });
if (count < st.seen) st.seen = count;                                   // The count was reset (a new fight).
if (pn("RiposteFire") === 2) {                                          // The event has found the boss: the shadow arrives.
// A side is clear when no Invisible_Wall (in the player's height band) is between the boss and the shadow, or where the shadow stands.
const bodyBox = function (o) {      // The box of an object's collision mask (its hit boxes), in the scene: not its whole sprite frame.
let l = Infinity, r = -Infinity, t = Infinity, b = -Infinity;
for (const h of boxes) for (const v of h.vertices) { l = Math.min(l, v[0]); r = Math.max(r, v[0]); t = Math.min(t, v[1]); b = Math.max(b, v[1]); }
if (l === Infinity && o.getAABBLeft) { l = o.getAABBLeft(); r = o.getAABBRight(); t = o.getAABBTop(); b = o.getAABBBottom(); }
if (l === Infinity) { l = r = o.getCenterXInScene(); t = b = o.getCenterYInScene(); }
return { l: l, r: r, t: t, b: b };
const me = bodyBox(player), half = Math.max(8, (me.r - me.l) / 2), walls = (runtimeScene.getObjects("Invisible_Wall") || []).map(bodyBox);
const lo = Math.min(bx, bx + side * GAP) - half, hi = Math.max(bx, bx + side * GAP) + half;
return !walls.some(w => w.b > me.t && w.t < me.b && w.r > lo && w.l < hi);
if (obj.flipX) obj.flipX(side > 0);                                 // The art faces right: toward the boss when he is on the right.
st.shadows.push({ obj: obj, age: 0, struck: false, srcX: bx + side * GAP });
if (!s.struck && s.age >= STRIKE) { s.struck = true; if (!pv.get("IsDead").getAsBoolean()) { pv.get("RiposteSrcX").setNumber(s.srcX); pv.get("RiposteStrike").setNumber(1); } }
if (s.age >= LIFE || pv.get("IsDead").getAsBoolean()) { s.obj.deleteFromScene(runtimeScene); st.shadows.splice(i, 1); continue; }
const rise = Math.min(1, s.age / 0.04), fade = Math.min(1, (LIFE - s.age) / FADE);       // In at once, out over the last FADE seconds.
s.obj.setOpacity(Math.round(ALPHA * rise * fade * (0.85 + 0.15 * Math.sin(s.age * 90))));   // A ghostly flicker.
// Every swing of the player that HITS (Player.HasHitThisSwing turns true) is remembered: where he stood, which way he faced, which attack it was.
// ECHO_DELAY seconds later a fainter shadow appears on that spot and swings the same attack. At its slash frame it sets Player.EchoStrike (with the
// spot in Player.EchoX); the event below takes EchoMult times AttackDamage off an enemy within EchoReach px of that spot, health only, never posture.
// So an echo lands only if the boss is still there: a hit-and-run leaves it swinging at air. The echoes do not echo, and the tutorial has none.
const player = players[0], pv = player.getVariables(), g = runtimeScene.getGame().getVariables();

st.echoes.push({ wait: ECHO_DELAY, light: light, x: player.getX(), y: player.getY(), cx: player.getCenterXInScene(), flip: !!(player.isFlippedX && player.isFlippedX()), scale: player.getScaleX(), obj: null, age: 0, struck: false });
const e = st.echoes[i], strikeAt = e.light ? 0.16 : 0.14, life = e.light ? 0.4 : 0.5;
if (!e.struck && e.age >= strikeAt) { e.struck = true; pv.get("EchoX").setNumber(e.cx); pv.get("EchoStrike").setNumber(1); }
const rise = Math.min(1, e.age / 0.04), fade = Math.min(1, (life - e.age) / 0.2);
// A DEFLECTED arrow of the Leaf Ranger or thrown blade of the Bladekeeper flies back at the boss as a bolt (Player_Return_Shot) and takes ReturnMult
// times AttackDamage of health off him on arrival (never posture), with the player's hit sound and blood. (The Gunslinger's parried bullets already fly
// back at him by themselves, and area attacks, beams, cuts and the Samurai's tornado and petals are not projectiles that can be returned.)
// No boss script is touched: every frame the projectiles of RETURNABLE are watched. A deflect is when Player.DeflectBlocked turns true and a watched
// projectile near the player (within NEAR px, seen last frame) is gone or has HasHit set; the player's HP did not fall on that frame (a hit is not a
// deflect). Player.BossX/BossY (an event writes them every frame) are where the bolt flies. On arrival it sets Player.ReturnStrike and
// Player.ReturnSrcX (where the bolt was, for the blood); the event below does the damage. The tutorial has none.
const player = players[0], pv = player.getVariables(), g = runtimeScene.getGame().getVariables();
const RETURNABLE = ["Ranger_Arrow", "Bladekeeper_Blade"], NEAR = 170, SPEED = 1100, HIT_DIST = 50, LIFE = 2;
if (!st.seenProj) st.seenProj = new Map(), st.shots = [], st.wasBlocked = blocked, st.lastHp = hp;
for (const name of RETURNABLE) for (const o of runtimeScene.getObjects(name) || []) {
const hit = o.getVariables().get("HasHit").getAsBoolean(), x = o.getCenterXInScene(), y = o.getCenterYInScene();
if (hit && was && !was.done) {                                       // It just hit something: the player (or his sword).
if (deflected && brand >= 4 && !dead && Math.hypot(was.x - px, was.y - py) < NEAR) st.spawn = (st.spawn || []).concat([[x, y]]);
} else if (!hit) st.seenProj.set(o, { x: x, y: y, done: false });
for (const [o, was] of Array.from(st.seenProj)) if (!alive.has(o)) {   // Gone this frame (deleted by its own boss events).
if (!was.done && deflected && brand >= 4 && !dead && Math.hypot(was.x - px, was.y - py) < NEAR) st.spawn = (st.spawn || []).concat([[was.x, was.y]]);
for (const [sx, sy] of st.spawn || []) {                               // A returned bolt starts where the projectile was.
if (obj) { obj.setZOrder(player.getZOrder() + 2); st.shots.push({ obj: obj, x: sx, y: sy, age: 0 }); }
const dx = bx - s.x, dy = by - s.y, d = Math.hypot(dx, dy);
if (dead || s.age > LIFE) { s.obj.deleteFromScene(runtimeScene); st.shots.splice(i, 1); continue; }
if (d <= HIT_DIST || d <= SPEED * dt) {                              // It arrives.
s.x += dx / d * SPEED * dt; s.y += dy / d * SPEED * dt;
// Switches it on for the events, which cannot read the global brand count: Player.RollDeflectOn is 1 from 5 brands (not in the tutorial). With it the
// sword can block the Samurai's grab, but only in the perfect window of a deflect (PerfectFractionNow): the grab whiffs and he is open. (Dodging is its
// own reward: a roll, the Flash step or the Wraith dash still just avoids a grab, the Cat's dash, landing and eruption, with no bonus on top.)
// A hit that would take the player's HP to 0 forms a metal coating instead (the event "Metal coat:" in Combat_Shared, before "Player loses a life"): he is
// healed MetalCoatHeal of his max HP, no life is lost and no curse stack taken, the boss flinches (JustStaggered: every boss stops what it is doing) and is
// knocked back MetalCoatKnock px, and the respawn invulnerability covers him for a moment. It can happen COAT_USES times per playthrough: the count is saved in
// the progress (SoulRush.progress.metalCoatUsed, wiped with the rest by Start over), so a retry does not bring it back. This script:
//   - works out Player.MetalCoatReady every frame (the power is in the global PowersOwned, uses are left, he is alive; not in the tutorial or the hub),

//   - when the event sets Player.MetalCoatFire, spends a use (saves it), turns him dark steel with a travelling shine (then fades back), plays a clang, sends two shockwave rings out and shows a mark above him,
//   - shows a small steel shield with a pip per use left, to the right of the HP bar, while the coat is ready (the buff icon),
//   - debug key Y (behind the DEBUG_KEYS gate): owns Metal coat for this fight and gives one use back (a stack), to try it without sparing the Bladekeeper.
const player = players[0], pv = player.getVariables(), g = runtimeScene.getGame().getVariables();
const store = () => { try { return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || "null") || { awakened: {}, beaten: {} }; } catch (e) { return { awakened: {}, beaten: {} }; } };
try { const p = store(); p.metalCoatUsed = st.coatUsed; localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(p)); } catch (e) { /* the use still counts for this fight */ }
st.coat = { age: 0, text: null, rings: null, x: player.getCenterXInScene(), y: player.getCenterYInScene() };
if (typeof PIXI !== "undefined" && PIXI.Graphics) {                                   // Two steel shockwave rings from where he stood.
st.coat.rings = [{ delay: 0, w: 7, color: 0xe8f0fa }, { delay: 0.1, w: 4, color: 0x8fa3bd }].map(r => { const g = new PIXI.Graphics(); g.zIndex = 1000001; root.addChild(g); r.g = g; return r; });

st.coat.text = new PIXI.Text("METAL COAT  (" + Math.max(0, COAT_USES - st.coatUsed) + " left)", { fontFamily: "Georgia, serif", fontSize: 20, fontWeight: "bold", fill: 0xc9d8e8, stroke: 0x000000, strokeThickness: 4 });
try { const p = store(); p.metalCoatUsed = st.coatUsed; localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(p)); } catch (e) { /* this fight only */ }
const ready = owned && live && st.coatUsed < COAT_USES;
// The buff icon: a steel shield right of the HP bar (UI layer), one pip per use left. Drawn again only when the number of uses changes.
gr.x = 352; gr.y = 17; gr.zIndex = 800000; root.addChild(gr); st.coatIcon = { gr: gr, shown: -1 };
const left = ready ? COAT_USES - st.coatUsed : 0, gr = st.coatIcon.gr;
gr.lineStyle(0); gr.beginFill(0x8fa3bd, 0.9); gr.drawPolygon([4, 4, 14, 4, 14, 24, 4, 14]); gr.endFill();   // The lit half of the plate.
for (let i = 0; i < COAT_USES; i++) { gr.beginFill(i < left ? 0xe8f0fa : 0x1c222c, 1); gr.drawCircle(37, 8 + i * 13, 4); gr.endFill(); }
gr.alpha = st.coat ? 0.55 + 0.45 * Math.sin(st.coat.age * 14) : 1;                // It flickers while the coat has just formed.
if (st.coat) {                                                           // The steel look: dark steel with a travelling shine, then it fades; the mark rises; shockwave rings.
const age = st.coat.age, HOLD = 0.9, FADE_T = 0.8, k = age <= HOLD ? 0 : Math.min(1, (age - HOLD) / FADE_T), mix = (a, c, u) => Math.round(a + (c - a) * u);
const shine = Math.max(0, Math.sin(age * 11 - 1.2)) * (1 - k), u = Math.max(k, 0);              // shine: 0 to 1, a glint sweeping through the steel.
if (player.setColor) player.setColor(mix(mix(95, 255, u), 255, shine * 0.95) + ";" + mix(mix(115, 255, u), 255, shine * 0.95) + ";" + mix(mix(150, 255, u), 255, shine * 0.95));

if (st.coat.text) { st.coat.text.x = player.getCenterXInScene(); st.coat.text.y = player.getCenterYInScene() - 70 - 30 * Math.min(1, age / 1.7); st.coat.text.alpha = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (1.7 - age) / 0.8)); }
const p = Math.min(1, ra / 0.45); r.g.visible = p < 1; r.g.clear();
if (p < 1) { r.g.lineStyle(r.w * (1 - p) + 1, r.color, 0.85 * (1 - p) * (1 - p)); r.g.drawCircle(0, 0, 22 + 170 * (1 - Math.pow(1 - p, 2))); r.g.x = st.coat.x; r.g.y = st.coat.y; }
if (st.coat.rings) for (const r of st.coat.rings) if (r.g.destroy) r.g.destroy();

Riposte: the shadow's slash lands. Health only, no posture, and not while the enemy is invulnerable. Adds a little hit-stop and shake like a hit.
Hit effects: the player's own hit sound and blood, from the shadow's side (the blood flies away from it).

It takes EchoMult times AttackDamage of health (never posture) off an enemy within EchoReach px of that spot, so it lands only if the boss is still there.
Hit effects: the player's own hit sound and blood, from the shadow's side (the blood flies away from it).
Boss info for the powers, HP: Player.BossHpFrac is the enemy's HP as a fraction of its max (BossVulnerable, next, is 1 while it is not invulnerable).
Boss info for the powers, vulnerable: BossVulnerable is 1.
Boss info for the powers, invulnerable: BossVulnerable is 0.

Hit effects: the player's own hit sound and blood, from the shadow's side (the blood flies away from it).
Poison stab: clear the flag (also when the boss could not be hurt).

Poison stab, the poison: while StabPoison lasts, the enemy's posture regen timer is held at zero every frame, so its posture cannot recover (this event runs before the regen event). The time counts down.

If the enemy is at or under RequiemHpFracNow of its max (RequiemHpFrac, or a huge number while debug key J has Requiem unlimited; the power checked that the boss was vulnerable when R was pressed and the game has been frozen since, so nothing can have changed): its HP drops to 1 and its posture is filled, so the posture-break event below runs at once and the boss drops into its stunned, kneeling stance with the deathblow orb as soon as time resumes, on every life. The player finishes it with F (the deathblow takes the life and heals him, and on the last life gives the mercy choice). A hard shake (no hit-stop: the whole sequence is frozen already), and the player's own hit sound and blood.
Hit effects: the player's own hit sound and blood, from the shadow's side (the blood flies away from it).
Requiem: clear the flag (also when the boss was no longer vulnerable).

Projectile return (brand 4): a bolt from a deflected arrow or thrown blade (the script above) arrived: it takes ReturnMult times AttackDamage of health (never posture) off the enemy, with the player's hit sound and blood.

Riposte: clear the request flag (also when no enemy was there to find).

Powers: R uses the selected power of the loadout (the hub writes LoadoutSlot1 to LoadoutSlot3), a tap of E selects the next one, and the selection and the last message show bottom left. Blood pact (the Gunslinger's kill power) pays BloodPactCost of max HP as sacrificed HP and refills stamina. Not in the tutorial or the hub. Debug key X equips Blood pact for this fight (remove before release).

inlineCode: // Powers in a fight (docs/design-brand-mercy.md, phase 4, slice 2). One script event in Combat_Shared, every frame. The hub works out the
// loadout and writes it into the globals LoadoutSlot1 to LoadoutSlot3 (tools/powers/powers.js, the altar screen picks them). Here:
//   R        uses the SELECTED power (the first filled slot at the start of a fight).
//   E (tap)  selects the next filled slot. A tap is a press shorter than a quarter of a second, so the mercy hold (one second) never counts.
//   J        (debug) toggles UNLIMITED actives: Requiem with no once-per-fight limit and at any boss HP, and no cooldowns at all (Poison stab, Blood pact); range and vulnerability still count.
//   X        (debug) puts the next built active in slot 1 for this fight (Blood pact, Requiem, Poison stab, then round again), to try them without earning them.
// The tutorial and the hub are exempt: no powers there. The selected power and a message show bottom left. Each power below says what it
// needs and does; paying in HP goes through Player.SacrificeHP (an event in this sheet takes it off, never kills, and rally cannot win it back).
const player = players[0], pv = player.getVariables(), g = runtimeScene.getGame().getVariables(), input = gdjs.evtTools.input;
const st = runtimeScene.__powers || (runtimeScene.__powers = { sel: -1, eDown: 0, cool: {}, msg: "", msgLeft: 0, hud: null, shown: "" });
const pn = k => pv.get(k).getAsNumber(), pb = k => pv.get(k).getAsBoolean();
// The powers. use(): returns a message to show, or "" when it did nothing.

// Poison stab (the Leaf Ranger's kill power): a SEMI-RANGED arrow stab (StabRange 420 px: an emergency posture stop). Within StabRange px of a boss that can be hurt, the player lunges an arrow into him (a short
// lock, about 0.45 s); at the strike Player.StabFire goes to 1 and the event in Combat_Shared (tools/brand) does a small hit (StabDamageMult of his damage,
// with the hit sound and blood) and starts StabPoison (StabPoisonTime s), during which the boss's posture CANNOT recover (its regen timer is held at zero each frame).
// Strong against the Samurai, whose posture recovers fast at full HP. Cooldown 14 s. A boss that cannot be hurt at the strike takes nothing (a whiff).
if (pn("BossVulnerable") !== 1) return "Too early: he cannot be hurt now";
if (Math.abs(pn("BossX") - player.getCenterXInScene()) > pn("StabRange")) return "Too far from him";
st.stab = { age: 0, started: false, struck: false, arrow: null, dir: player.getCenterXInScene() < pn("BossX") ? 1 : -1 };
// Requiem (brand 3): the big one-time slash. Close to the boss (RequiemRange px) and with him at or under RequiemHpFrac of his HP (this life), once per
// fight. The GAME IS FROZEN for the whole sequence (the time scale goes to 0.0001; only the shadow, the camera and the effects move, on real time), so the boss

// cannot dash away or dodge between the press and the cut: it always lands where he stood. The player is locked and untouchable while the camera zooms in, his shadow (big) cuts the boss, and at the strike Player.RequiemFire

// goes to 1 (the sequence is about 2.5 s: long enough to take in): the event in Combat_Shared (tools/brand) leaves the boss at 1 HP with his posture broken, so he drops into the stunned kneel at once and the player finishes him with the deathblow (F).
// Player.BossX, BossHpFrac and BossVulnerable are written every frame by events (tools/brand).
if (st.requiemUsed && !st.requiemDebug) return "Requiem is spent for this fight";
if (pn("BossVulnerable") !== 1) return "Too early: he cannot be hurt now";

events.comment: Enemy posture recovers while it is above zero and not broken, starting PostureRegenDelay seconds after the last hit (1.5 for most bosses; 0 means it is always going down, even while he is being hit: the Leaf Ranger). The rate depends on his HP: PostureRegenEmpty per second at 0 HP up to PostureRegenFull per second at full HP, so a healthy Samurai recovers fast and a wounded one slowly. Bosses that want a flat rate set both to the same number (the default is 5 and 5, as it always was).
Keep enemy posture within its maximum.
Enemy dodges this hit: no damage. Sets JustDodgedHit so the boss can react.

Player hits the enemy, once per swing: damage, posture (only if Enemy.MeleeDamagesPosture is true), blood, rally healing, and a hit sound. Sets JustHitByPlayer for the boss's events. Skipped while Enemy.Invulnerable is true. Also adds hit-stop and screen shake.
Melee posture: only for bosses with MeleeDamagesPosture on. The Gunslinger has it off, so sword hits only cost it health and its posture comes from parried bullets.
The hit came from a lunge: add LungeBonusDamage and set JustStaggered for the boss events.

Blood, the roll: one of the 9 splashes (Blood1 to Blood9, tools/fx/blood.js) and a size from 1 to 1.4. Two of them are fountains with no direction, the rest spray to the right and are flipped below for a hit from the right, so the blood always flies away from the player. A lunge hits harder, so its blood is bigger.
Blood, a lunge: bigger.
Blood, the player is left of the enemy: the splash starts on the enemy's near side and flies to the right.
Blood, the player is right of the enemy: the same, flipped, flying to the left.
Enemy posture break: starts the stun and sets JustPostureBroken for the boss's events. Also adds a strong hit-stop and screen shake.
Enemy stun ends after Enemy.StunDuration seconds and sets JustRecovered for the boss's events.

Deathblow: press F in melee range of a posture-broken enemy. The player winds up, then cuts. The cut removes one enemy life, and one curse stack lifts as the life wisps reach the player. The player is locked and cannot be hit until it finishes. Also adds a strong hit-stop and screen shake on the cut.
Enemy on the right: dash right.
Enemy on the left: dash left.
Wall check: pass through only if the landing spot, DeathblowPassDist past the enemy, is inside DeathblowMinX to DeathblowMaxX. Otherwise the cut happens in front of him and the player stays put.
Room behind the enemy: pass through.
Deathblow cut, on the dash frame: the hit itself, the orb shatter and the slash. The player then glows crimson as the life is taken.
Pass through: land DeathblowPassDist past the enemy, still facing the same way, so the player ends with their back to him. The slash runs from where they started to where they land.
Wall behind the enemy: no pass. The slash runs from the player across the enemy.
Deathblow: hold the follow-through, blade forward, for DeathblowHold seconds.
Deathblow: the hold is over, so he raises the blade, slowly, to clean it.
Deathblow: the blade is up. Pause there for DeathblowRaiseHold seconds, the moment before the flick.
Deathblow: the pause is over, so flick the blood off in one fast swish, then settle.
Deathblow finished: give control back.

Deathblow glow: for DeathblowGlowTime seconds the player glows crimson, fading back, as the stolen life flows in. When it ends, one curse stack lifts and HP refills (DeathblowLanded, handled by the curse removal event below).
Early in the glow: deep crimson.
Later in the glow: fading toward normal.
Glow over: back to normal, and the life lands.
Remove the orb shatter and the slash when their animations end.
Remove the slash when its animation ends.
Deathblow prompt: the orb, hidden by default. Uses the same conditions as the deathblow, minus the key press.
Deathblow prompt: show the orb just above the enemy's head when a deathblow is possible. Enemy.DeathblowOrbDrop lowers it for a boss whose stunned pose is shorter than its collision box.
Enemy loses a life at 0 HP and sets JustLostLife. On its last life it is deleted, or sets JustDied if HasDeathAnimation is on.

Debug, left Alt: toggle Desperation. On: put the player on his last life with every curse stack (4 of the 5 lives lost, 15% max HP each, full HP of what is left), and remember what he had (DbgLives, DbgCurse, DbgMaxHealth, DbgHealth). Off (press again): give those back. The next hit kills while it is on. Remove before release (DEBUG_KEYS). DbgSnap is taken first, so the on and off events cannot both run in one frame (the off event used to undo the on event at once).

Debug, L: toggle permanent Desperation. On: the Desperation window is always at its maximum (as if the player had every curse stack) and every deflect that lands counts as a Desperation deflect (teal blade, icon pulse). Off: back to the real curse stacks. Switched off by the DEBUG_KEYS gate.

Debug, P: toggle forced perfect deflects (Player.PerfectForced). While it is on, every deflect that lands counts as a perfect one, whatever the timing, to test the powers that read it. Remove before release (DEBUG_KEYS).

Desperation: the curse's silver lining. Each curse stack, up to DesperationMax (3), widens the deflect window by DesperationStep (0.02 s), so a struggling player gets a little more forgiveness. Boss timings are unchanged, and the curse still costs max HP, so dying is never the better way to play. Both deflects (this sheet's and the Gunslinger's) read DeflectWindowNow; the icon is drawn by the fight UI layout below.

parameters: Player.Variable(DeflectWindow) + Player.Variable(DesperationStep) * min(max(Player.Variable(CurseStacks), Player.Variable(DespForced) * Player.Variable(DesperationMax)), Player.Variable(DesperationMax))

events.comment: Directional deflecting, for every fight: a deflect only counts when the player faces the boss (facing left means FlippedX). FacingOk is 1 unless the player has their back to him. Not applied (stays 1) when DirectionalDeflect on the Player is 0, when the boss has DeflectAnySide 1 (his sheet sets it while an attack comes from several sides, for example the boss is hidden or dead), or when he is within 40 px sideways. Each attack also has its own Directional variable (1 normal, 0 for attacks that come from all around, like the petals and the arrow rain), read by the deflect event below. The side an attack comes from is the boss, unless his sheet sets AimX (0 or more) to the x of whoever is attacking right now, for example the Samurai's illusion: then the player has to face that figure.

Deflect: an enemy attack that reaches the player within DeflectWindowNow seconds (DeflectWindow, widened by Desperation) of raising the sword is stopped, with a random clash sound and a burst of sparks (one of the Deflect_Spark animations, picked at random). Setting HasHit makes the damage event below skip it. All enemy attacks go through this, including each Thousand Cuts slash. Also adds hit-stop and screen shake. One press stops any number of melee attacks, but only one ranged attack (DeflectRangedUsed), so each arrow of a double shot needs its own deflect. Both branches of that Or name EnemyHitbox and Player on purpose: an Or only keeps the objects its true branches picked, so a branch that left one out would drop it (no arrow blocked, or no Player to act on). A hitbox with SharedDeflect 1 (the Samurai's paired mirror cuts, his waves of petals) does not use up the press: it counts like a melee attack for this, but adds no posture, so one deflect stops everything of that kind that reaches the player in the window. Directional deflecting: unless the attack's Directional variable is 0, the press only counts when the player faces the boss (Player.FacingOk, worked out just above).

Deflect sound: one of the 21 echo clashes at random (7 pitches x 3 takes, made by tools/fx/clash.js), so repeated deflects never sound identical. Replaces sword_parry_01.wav. Also draws the new spark additively, so its glow lights up its surroundings.

inlineCode: // Deflect sound: a random echo clash. The files are deflect_clash_<pitch>_echo[_b|_c].wav in assets/Sfx,
// generated by tools/fx/clash.js (rerun it to change them). Volume 51: 40% under the old parry sound (85), which was too loud with these.
// Spark light: the new Deflect_Spark is drawn additively, so its glow halo brightens what is behind it like real light.
for (const s of runtimeScene.getObjects("Deflect_Spark")) if (!s.__lit) { s.__lit = true; s.setBlendMode(1); }

events.comment: Deflected a melee attack: it also adds DeflectPostureDamage to the enemy posture and stops posture recovery for a moment, like a hit does. Attacks with IsMelee off, such as ranged ones, add nothing. The posture is DeflectPostureDamage times the attack's PostureScale (1 normally; the Samurai's illusion swings with 0.5, half).
Deflected a ranged attack (an arrow, a rain hit): this press is used up for ranged attacks, so a second arrow close behind it needs its own deflect.

Desperation feedback: the deflect landed after the base DeflectWindow, so only the curse's extra window allowed it. Flag it for the blade glow and the icon pulse (a deflect inside the normal window shows nothing).
Desperation, forced (debug key L): every deflect that lands counts as a Desperation deflect: the blade turns teal and the icon pulses, whatever the timing.

Perfect deflect: the deflect landed within PerfectFractionNow (PerfectFraction, wider with Steady hand) of the base DeflectWindow (the first part of it, never Desperation's extra window), so Player.PerfectCount goes up by one. Powers read it by keeping their own seen number (PerfectCount above it), so it does not matter which event sheet runs first. PerfectForced (debug key P) makes every deflect count.

Perfect melee deflect: the same, for melee attacks only (EnemyHitbox.IsMelee): Player.PerfectMeleeCount goes up too. Riposte reads this one, so ranged attacks (the Samurai's tornado, Judgement Cut and Thousand Cuts, arrows, petals, grenades) never call the shadow.

Enemy attack hits the player once per attack object. Damage comes from that object's Damage variable, and JustHitPlayer is set for the boss's events. A hit also drops any saved action, cancels the player attack, deflect or roll (a roll only gets hit once its i-frames are over) and plays the Player_Hit reaction. Also adds hit-stop and screen shake. Nothing can hit the player during a grab, so a stray attack cannot break that animation.

Metal coat: the Bladekeeper's mercy gift. A hit that took the player's HP to 0 (and the script says he has the power and a use left: Player.MetalCoatReady) forms a metal coating instead of costing a life: he is healed MetalCoatHeal of his max HP, rally and posture are cleared, no life or curse stack is taken, the respawn invulnerability covers him, the enemy flinches (JustStaggered: it stops what it is doing) and slides MetalCoatKnock px away from him over KnockTime seconds (in a grab the coat breaks the grab: the player is released, and the grabbing boss's own sheet staggers it). A harder hit-stop and shake mark it. MetalCoatFire tells the script to spend the use (saved in the progress) and show the effect. This is in front of Player loses a life.

Metal coat, the flinch: the coat has just formed (MetalCoatFire) and the player was not grabbed: the enemy flinches (JustStaggered: it stops what it is doing) and is set sliding away. NOT when the enemy is invulnerable: that means it is in a protected sequence (the Samurai's ultimate, a grab, his phase intermission), which a flinch would break (the Samurai would stay invulnerable and the player locked). Those sequences are handled by their own boss sheets.

Metal coat, in a grab: the same, when the hit was a grab's stab (the player is IsGrabbed; the blade went in as a direct hit). The coat BREAKS the grab: the player is released at once into the idle pose and the boss slides away like any other. MetalCoatFire stays 1 for the rest of this frame, which is how the grabbing boss's own sheet knows to drop the grab (the Samurai's: Metal coat, the grab breaks, in samurai_boss.json).

Metal coat, the knockback: for KnockTime seconds the enemy slides away from the player (set when the coat formed), fast at first and slowing to a stop (an ease-out), MetalCoatKnock px in all. A slide, not a jump, so it reads as a shove and not a glitch.

Player loses a life: applies the curse (one more CurseStacks; max HP is the base minus the brands' loss and the curse stacks, never below the HP floor), clears rally and posture, and starts respawn invulnerability. On the last life, or when the stack breaches the floor, the player dies instead.

Curse breach: a curse stack that takes max HP below the HP floor (HpFloorPercent of the base) is fatal. The life count is set to 0, so the last-life-gone event below plays the death, and BreachDeath marks it for the ending. (A player with many brands cannot afford many curse stacks.)
Last life gone: play the death animation. The player is locked and cannot be hit, and the fade below returns to the hub.
End respawn invulnerability after 1.5 seconds.
Player death: DeathHold seconds after the collapse, fade the screen to black over DeathFadeTime seconds.

Player death fade: darken the screen and keep the overlay over the camera. The fade stops at 170 of 255: a dark overlay over the scene (the fallen player and the fight still show through), not a black screen; the death menu opens over it.
Player death fade is black: the death menu asks Try again (reload this fight) or Return to the hub. The player is never sent back to the hub on their own.

events.comment: Sacrificed HP: a power that pays in HP sets Player.SacrificeHP. The HP comes off at once, never kills (at least 1 is left), and is not written into the rally pool, so rally cannot win it back. The deathblow's refill still restores it.
Player status, root: while RootLeft lasts the player cannot move, roll or lunge, but can still attack and deflect. Player_Movement checks IsRooted.
Root over.

Every half second: lose PoisonTick HP. PoisonAcc counts the time, because a timer that was never started never passes its check.
Poison over: back to the normal colour.
Debug: F5 restarts the current scene. Remove before release.

const FADE = 1.2; // Seconds for the fade to black.

for (const name of st.names) for (const o of runtimeScene.getObjects(name)) {

if (dying > 0 && st.settle < MAX_SETTLE) { st.settle += dt; return; }
